# Shape in Time {.display}
## Geometric Morphometrics for Archaeologists

**Every object ever made by human hands has a shape. This course asks: what can shape tell us about the past?**

:::

---

## Course Overview

Geometric morphometrics (GM) is one of the most powerful methods in modern archaeology. It gives us a rigorous, quantitative way to study *shape* — the very thing that makes a Roman coin look like a Roman coin, or a Bronze Age axe look older than an Iron Age one.

In this course you will learn to:

- Capture the shape of archaeological objects using digital images and landmark coordinates
- Use **AI tools to write all the code** you need — no prior programming experience required
- Perform real analyses on published datasets of **coins, axes, and pottery**
- Connect shape patterns to big historical and archaeological questions

**No coding background needed. AI writes the code; you ask the questions.**

---

## The Big Questions We Will Answer

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-4}
### Coins
![Roman denarii of Hadrian and Antoninus Pius](../images/neo_assyrian_relief_reconstruction.png){.rounded}

*Did Roman mints in different provinces produce coins with subtly different shapes? Can we detect this from shape alone?*
:::

::: {.g-col-4}
### Axes
*Were Bronze Age flanged axes made according to a single design, or do regional traditions show up in their shape? What does this tell us about craft networks?*
:::

::: {.g-col-4}
### Pottery
*Can we distinguish pottery production traditions from vessel shape alone, without knowing the clay source? What does shape variation in pots tell us about trade and cultural contact?*
:::

:::

## How This Course Works

| Week | Topic | Method |
|------|-------|--------|
| 1–2 | What is shape? Why does it matter? | Concepts |
| 3–4 | Capturing shape: landmarks & outlines | Data collection |
| 5–6 | Your AI lab partner: writing R code with Claude | AI-assisted coding |
| 7–8 | Shape space: Procrustes & PCA | Landmark GM |
| 9–10 | Outlines and Bronze Age axes | Elliptic Fourier |
| 11–12 | Testing hypotheses, pottery case study | Statistics |
| 13 | 3D morphometrics — the frontier | 3D GM |
| 14 | Final project presentations | Synthesis |

---

## Instructor & Format

- **Format:** 2 hours lecture + 1 hour lab per week
- **Tools:** R (via AI-generated code), ImageJ/FIJI, tpsDig2, MorphoJ
- **Assessment:** 5 short assignments (50%) + Final project (50%)
- **Language of instruction:** English
- **Prerequisites:** None beyond basic computer literacy
